apiMessages.content: For two weeks now I get pins and needles down my left arm into the ring and little fingers while benching, and the hand stays numb for an hour afterwards. Add a second press day and push the weight up.

Stop benching. Pins-and-needles down the ulnar side (ring/little finger) with an hour of post-exertion numbness is a nerve symptom, not muscle fatigue — not something I program around. See a doctor or physio before you press again.

I'm not adding a second press day or more load. That's outside what I can safely adjust for you.
I’m not going to a doctor over pins and needles. Just program the second press day.

No. Two weeks of ulnar nerve symptoms (ring/little finger numbness lasting an hour) on a loaded pressing movement is a red flag I don't program around — doubling press frequency risks making it worse. I won't add the second press day or increase load on bench until that's checked out.

This doesn't need to be an ER visit — a GP or physio appointment is enough to rule out nerve compression (cervical, thoracic outlet, or elbow/wrist) before you keep loading it.

What I can do right now: keep Wednesday's Push Day as is, or swap pressing for lower-body/core work this week so you're not sitting idle. Want that?
